$comment: Explicit, reviewed exemptions from scripts/check-public-safety.mjs's opaque-content refusal (issue #588). A PDF, image, font, video, or wasm file (see OPAQUE_EXTENSIONS in that script) is refused by default: this gate cannot deterministically parse those formats, so it can never prove one carries no private identity or credential-shaped content, and 'cannot prove clean' must never become 'counted as clean'. An entry below is a human's recorded review of one EXACT file -- `path` is its repository-relative path (matched the same way a denylist neutralize rule's `paths` is, so one entry covers both the tree scan and the packed-tarball scan of the same file), `sha256` is the sha256 of its exact bytes, `reason` (at least 20 characters) says what was actually checked and why the file is safe, and `issue` is the integer issue this exemption is tracked against. This mirrors scripts/check-package-evidence.mjs's `gaps` mechanism, including its rule that an acknowledgement must not outlive its reason: here that is enforced by the hash rather than by re-derived evidence -- change a single byte of the file and its sha256 no longer matches any entry here, so the exemption stops applying and the file is refused again until it is reviewed again.

exemptions.reason: Exact bytes match the existing 542-byte VP9 fixture; owner approved this opaque artifact for shipment on 2026-10-30 acknowledging opaque-content limits. No replacement or re-encoding.
